question:
The following sentence contains an error. Select the option that correctly rectifies the error.

If I was a king, I would have tried my best to remove poverty from my country.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. If I were a king,.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence expresses an unreal / imaginary condition (a wish contrary to fact). In the second/third conditional, the verb "be" takes the subjunctive form "were" for all subjects — so "If I were a king", not "If I was a king".

◦ Correct: If I were a king, I would have tried my best to remove poverty from my country.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "on my country" (should be "from my country") is already correct in the sentence; "my best by remove poverty" and "I would has tried" are wrong distractors.

• With "would have + V3", the "if" clause needs the past subjunctive "were".

NOTE

• The subjunctive mood uses "were" for hypothetical/unreal ideas: "If I were you", "I wish I were rich", "As if he were a genius". (काल्पनिक स्थिति में 'were')

question:
Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

The manager decided to disclose a secret and address the issue at the team meeting.
option_3: hit the nail on the head
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. spill the beans.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "spill the beans" means to reveal/disclose a secret (often unintentionally). It fits "disclose a secret". (राज़ खोल देना)

◦ Correct: The manager decided to spill the beans and address the issue at the team meeting.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "bury the hatchet" = to make peace / end a quarrel.

• Option 3 "hit the nail on the head" = to describe exactly what is causing a situation.

• Option 4 "sweep it under the rug" = to hide/ignore a problem.

NOTE

• Similar idioms of revealing: "let the cat out of the bag", "give the game away", "blow the whistle".

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

The blanket gifted by my granny is softer and cozy.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. soft.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The adjective "cozy" (positive degree) is joined by "and" to the first adjective, so both must be in the same degree. Since "cozy" is positive, the first should also be positive — "soft", giving "soft and cozy".

◦ Correct: The blanket gifted by my granny is soft and cozy.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "softer" (comparative) needs "than" and cannot be paired with the positive "cozy".

• "more soft" is a wrong double form; "softly" is an adverb; "softest" is superlative (needs "the").

NOTE

• When two adjectives describe one noun and are joined by "and", keep them parallel in degree: soft and cozy / softer and cozier / softest and coziest. (समान डिग्री)

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

They was / celebrating their / Silver wedding anniversary / next month in Dubai.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. They was.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The subject "They" is plural, so it takes the plural verb "were", not the singular "was". So it should be "They were celebrating".

◦ Correct: They were celebrating their Silver wedding anniversary next month in Dubai.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "celebrating their", "Silver wedding anniversary" and "next month in Dubai" are all grammatically correct.

• "were celebrating" (past continuous) also works with a future arrangement here.

NOTE

• Subject–verb agreement: I/He/She/It → was; We/You/They → were. (कर्ता-क्रिया मेल)

question:
Select the word that has the same meaning (SYNONYM) as the underlined word in the given sentence.

Almost as wide as he was tall, he had a voracious appetite for food and drink and a rollicking personality to match.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. insatiable.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Voracious" means having a very great appetite; extremely eager/greedy for food (or something). Its closest synonym is "insatiable" (impossible to satisfy). (अतृप्त / भूखा)

◦ Example: He had a voracious/insatiable appetite for food.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "vehement" (showing strong feeling), Option 2 "imminent" (about to happen) and Option 4 "venerable" (deserving respect due to age) are unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of voracious: insatiable, ravenous, greedy, gluttonous, avid. Antonyms: satisfied, moderate. "A voracious reader" = one who reads a great deal.

question:
Select the option that rectifies the spelling of the underlined word in the given sentence.

The police informed the statesman that the goons were up to something mischievious.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. mischievous.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "mischievous" (mis-chie-vous), meaning causing or intending to cause trouble/harm in a playful way. (शरारती)

◦ Spelling key: MIS + CHIE + VOUS (no extra "i" after "v").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "mischievious", "mischevious", "mischeivous" and "mischevous" are all common misspellings.

NOTE

• Word family: mischief (noun), mischievous (adjective), mischievously (adverb). Note the "ie" in mischief and mischievous. (वर्तनी)

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

The unexpected guest at the party was a bull in a China shop.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. careless and damaging.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "a bull in a china shop" describes a clumsy, careless person who causes damage or handles a delicate situation roughly. So it means "careless and damaging". (अनाड़ी / फूहड़)

◦ Correct sense: The unexpected guest was careless and damaging.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "influential and meticulous", Option 3 "careful and compassionate" and Option 4 "leisurely and relaxed" are the opposite of the idiom's meaning.

NOTE

• A "bull in a china shop" acts without care in a place needing gentleness. Related idea: "like a wrecking ball" — causing destruction.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

By next summer, they will be _____ their house.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. renovating.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• After "will be", the present participle (V-ing) is required to form the future continuous tense. So "will be renovating". (भविष्य सतत काल)

◦ Correct: By next summer, they will be renovating their house.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "renovates" (present simple), "renovate" (base form) and "renovated" (past/participle) do not fit after "will be" in an active continuous structure.

NOTE

• Future continuous = will be + V-ing (will be working, will be travelling). It shows an action in progress at a future time. (will be + V-ing)

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

She treats her juniors _____ contempt.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. with.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct collocation is "treat someone with contempt" — the preposition "with" is used to show the manner/attitude. (तिरस्कार के साथ)

◦ Correct: She treats her juniors with contempt.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "by", "in" and "for" are not used with "treat ... contempt".

• "With" commonly follows "treat" to describe attitude: treat with respect/kindness/care/contempt.

NOTE

• Useful collocations: "treat with respect", "look upon with contempt", "hold in contempt", "beneath contempt".

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word..
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Oppertunity.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Oppertunity" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "Opportunity", meaning a favourable chance or occasion. (अवसर)

◦ Spelling key: OP + POR + TU + NI + TY (with "or", not "er").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Appearance", "Immigration" and "Astronaut" are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Remember: opportunity (double "p", "or" in the middle). Related word: "opportune" (well-timed). (वर्तनी)

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Chaotic
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Systematic.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Chaotic" means in a state of complete disorder and confusion. Its antonym is "systematic", meaning done according to an organised plan or method. (अव्यवस्थित का विलोम — व्यवस्थित)

◦ Example: The chaotic office became systematic after the new manager arrived.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Confused" is a synonym of chaotic.

• Options 2 "Dressed" and 3 "Obscure" (unclear) are unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of chaotic: disordered, confused, disorganised, turbulent. Antonyms: systematic, orderly, organised, methodical.

question:
The given sentence has an error. Select the option that rectifies the error.

The students were asked to turn up their assignments by Friday.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. turn in their assignments.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrasal verb "turn in" means to submit/hand in (work), which is the intended meaning. "Turn up" means "to appear/arrive" or "to increase", which does not fit here. So it should be "turn in their assignments".

◦ Correct: The students were asked to turn in their assignments by Friday.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "The students were asked to" and "their assignments by Friday" are already correct.

• "turn up" (arrive/appear) changes the meaning entirely.

NOTE

• Phrasal verbs with "turn": turn in (submit / go to bed), turn up (appear), turn down (reject), turn over (hand over / flip). (submit = turn in)

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Out of spirits
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Gloomy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "out of spirits" means feeling low, sad, depressed or gloomy. (उदास / निराश)

◦ Example: He has been out of spirits since he failed the exam — i.e., gloomy.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Cheerful" is the opposite.

• Options 3 "Hurt" and 4 "Obsolete" (outdated) do not match.

NOTE

• Contrast: "in high spirits" = cheerful and lively; "out of spirits / low-spirited" = sad and gloomy.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the word 'Illuminate' from the given sentence.

The toughest and most typical question in the examination was to elucidate a particular theory related to friction in physics.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Elucidate.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Illuminate" (in the sense of making something clear) means to explain / throw light on / clarify. Its synonym in the sentence is "elucidate", which means to make something clear by explaining it. (स्पष्ट करना)

◦ Example: The teacher tried to illuminate/elucidate the difficult theory.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Typical" (representative), Option 3 "Particular" (specific) and Option 4 "Theory" (an idea/principle) are not synonyms of "illuminate".

NOTE

• Synonyms of illuminate/elucidate: explain, clarify, clear up, throw light on, expound. Antonyms: obscure, confuse.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution required'.

Everyone in the room was in a jolly and relaxed mood.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. No substitution required.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence is already grammatically correct. "in a jolly and relaxed mood" uses the positive adjective "jolly" correctly, parallel with "relaxed". No comparative or superlative is needed. So "No substitution required".

◦ Correct: Everyone in the room was in a jolly and relaxed mood.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "most jolly" (superlative) and "jollier" (comparative) would break the positive-degree parallel with "relaxed".

• "more jollier" is a wrong double comparative.

NOTE

• Never combine "more" with the "-er" comparative form ("more jollier" is incorrect). Positive adjectives pair with positive: "jolly and relaxed".

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined word in the given sentence.

Urban people have a bombastic lifestyle, which is very different from those of rural folks.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Pretentious.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Bombastic" means high-sounding, showy and pompous; using inflated language or an ostentatious/pretentious manner. So its meaning here is "pretentious". (आडंबरपूर्ण / दिखावटी)

◦ Example: His bombastic/pretentious speech was full of grand but empty words.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Hollow" (empty), Option 3 "Delusive" (deceptive) and Option 4 "Common" (ordinary) do not correctly define bombastic.

NOTE

• Synonyms of bombastic: pretentious, pompous, grandiose, ostentatious, flamboyant. Antonyms: modest, simple, unpretentious.

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Occassion.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Occassion" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "Occasion" (double "c", single "s"), meaning a particular event or a special/important time. (अवसर)

◦ Spelling key: OC + CA + SION.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "Efficient", "Boundary" and "Illustration" are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Remember: occasion has double "c" and single "s". Related: occasional, occasionally. (वर्तनी)

question:
Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

The new employee is really trying to fit in, but sometimes he feels out of place and uncomfortable.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. a fish out of water.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "a fish out of water" means a person who feels uncomfortable/out of place in an unfamiliar situation or environment. It fits "out of place and uncomfortable". (असहज / बेगाना महसूस करना)

◦ Correct: The new employee sometimes feels like a fish out of water.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "a diamond in the rough" = a person with hidden good qualities.

• Option 2 "a bird of a feather" = people of similar type ("birds of a feather flock together").

• Option 4 "a needle in a haystack" = something very hard to find.

NOTE

• "A fish out of water" stresses discomfort in a new/strange setting. Opposite idea: "in one's element" (comfortable and happy).

question:
Select the word segment from the given options that substitutes the highlighted word segment correctly and completes the sentence meaningfully: -

Each of the participants were given a certificate.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. was given.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The subject is "Each of the participants". "Each" is a singular word and always takes a singular verb, so "were" is wrong and should be "was given".

◦ Correct: Each of the participants was given a certificate.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "have given"/"are given"/"have been given" are plural or wrong-voice forms that do not agree with the singular subject "each".

• Passive singular: "was given" (a certificate was given to each).

NOTE

• Singular subjects that take a singular verb: each, every, either, neither, one of. "Each of the boys is present." (Each + singular verb)

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Captivity
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Liberty.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Captivity" means the state of being imprisoned or confined. Its antonym is "liberty", meaning freedom. (कैद का विलोम — स्वतंत्रता)

◦ Example: After years of captivity, the animals were released to liberty.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Ethnicity" (belonging to a social group), Option 3 "Entity" (a thing that exists) and Option 4 "Authenticity" (genuineness) are unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of captivity: confinement, imprisonment, bondage, incarceration. Antonyms: liberty, freedom, release, emancipation.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

In recent years, the central and state governments in India have been taking special steps to __1__ foreign companies to invest in India. Industrial zones, called Special Economic Zones (SEZs), are being __2__. SEZs have world-class facilities, including electricity, water, roads, transport, storage, recreational, and educational facilities. Companies that set up production units in the SEZs do not have to pay taxes for an initial period of five years. The government has also __3__ flexibility in the labour laws to attract foreign investment. In recent years, the government has allowed companies to __4__ many of these provisions. Instead of hiring workers on a regular basis, companies hire workers 'flexibly' for short periods when there is __5__ pressure of work. This is done to reduce the cost of labour for the company. However, some foreign companies are not satisfied, and they are demanding more in labour laws, citing the need for greater operational efficiency.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. attract.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The governments are taking steps to "attract" foreign companies to invest — i.e., to draw them in / persuade them to come. This fits the theme of encouraging foreign investment. (आकर्षित करना)

◦ Correct: ... taking special steps to attract foreign companies to invest in India.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "fulfil" (to carry out), Option 3 "deplore" (to strongly disapprove) and Option 4 "abhor" (to hate) do not fit the positive sense of drawing investment.

NOTE

• "Attract investment / attract tourists / attract attention" are common collocations. Synonyms: draw, lure, entice. Antonyms: repel, deter.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Industrial zones, called Special Economic Zones (SEZs), are being __2__. SEZs have world-class facilities, including electricity, water, roads, transport, storage, recreational, and educational facilities. Companies that set up production units in the SEZs do not have to pay taxes for an initial period of five years. The government has also __3__ flexibility in the labour laws to attract foreign investment. In recent years, the government has allowed companies to __4__ many of these provisions. Instead of hiring workers on a regular basis, companies hire workers 'flexibly' for short periods when there is __5__ pressure of work. This is done to reduce the cost of labour for the company. However, some foreign companies are not satisfied, and they are demanding more in labour laws, citing the need for greater operational efficiency.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. set up.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Special Economic Zones (SEZs) are being "set up" — i.e., established/created. The passage then describes their world-class facilities, confirming they are being newly established. (स्थापित किया जाना)

◦ Correct: Industrial zones, called Special Economic Zones (SEZs), are being set up.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "dismantled" (taken apart) and Option 4 "wound up" (closed down) mean the opposite of establishing.

• Option 3 "obeyed" does not suit "zones".

NOTE

• Phrasal verb "set up" = to establish/start (a business, institution, zone). Antonyms: wind up, close down, dismantle.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

In recent years, the central and state governments in India have been taking special steps to __1__ foreign companies to invest in India. Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. allowed.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The government has "allowed" flexibility in the labour laws to attract foreign investment — i.e., permitted/given flexibility. (अनुमति देना)

◦ Correct: The government has also allowed flexibility in the labour laws ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "winked" (closed and opened an eye), Option 3 "invited" and Option 4 "suffered" do not collocate with "flexibility in the labour laws".

NOTE

• "Allow flexibility / allow access / allow time" are natural collocations. Synonyms of allow: permit, grant, let. Antonyms: forbid, prohibit.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

In recent years, the central and state governments in India have been taking special steps to __1__ foreign companies to invest in India. Industrial zones, called Special Economic Zones (SEZs), are being __2__. SEZs have world-class facilities, including electricity, water, roads, transport, storage, recreational, and educational facilities. Companies that set up production units in the SEZs do not have to pay taxes for an initial period of five years. Instead of hiring workers on a regular basis, companies hire workers 'flexibly' for short periods when there is __5__ pressure of work. This is done to reduce the cost of labour for the company. However, some foreign companies are not satisfied, and they are demanding more in labour laws, citing the need for greater operational efficiency.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. ignore.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The government has allowed companies to "ignore" many of these provisions — i.e., to disregard/not follow them. The next sentence (hiring workers 'flexibly' instead of on a regular basis) explains that the usual labour provisions are being set aside. (अनदेखा करना)

◦ Correct: ... the government has allowed companies to ignore many of these provisions.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "flounder" (to struggle), Option 3 "distort" (to twist) and Option 4 "effect" (to bring about) do not fit "provisions" in this context.

NOTE

• "Ignore rules / ignore provisions / ignore advice" — to pay no attention to. Synonyms: disregard, overlook, neglect. Antonyms: heed, observe, follow.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

In recent years, the central and state governments in India have been taking special steps to __1__ foreign companies to invest in India. However, some foreign companies are not satisfied, and they are demanding more in labour laws, citing the need for greater operational efficiency.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. intense.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Companies hire workers 'flexibly' for short periods when there is "intense" pressure of work — i.e., great/heavy pressure. This explains the need for extra short-term hiring. (तीव्र / अत्यधिक)

◦ Correct: ... for short periods when there is intense pressure of work.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "inadequate" (not enough), Option 3 "mechanical" and Option 4 "artificial" do not logically describe "pressure of work" here — heavy pressure is what causes extra hiring.

NOTE

• "Intense pressure / intense heat / intense competition" — very strong/extreme. Synonyms: severe, extreme, acute. Antonyms: mild, slight, moderate.

question: Who became the first woman to command the Armed Forces Transfusion Centre, Delhi Cantt, which is the largest blood transfusion centre of the Armed Forces in Nov 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Col Sunita BS.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In November 2023, Colonel Sunita BS became the first woman to command the Armed Forces Transfusion Centre (AFTC) at Delhi Cantt, the largest blood transfusion centre of the Armed Forces. (कर्नल सुनीता बी.एस.)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The AFTC collects, processes and supplies blood and blood products to armed forces hospitals across India.

• Her appointment marked a milestone for women in leadership roles in the Indian Army Medical Corps.

NOTE

• Women officers have been reaching many "firsts" in the armed forces recently, including command roles, fighter-pilot duties and permanent commission (following the 2020 Supreme Court verdict).

question: In which of the following classical dance forms are the actors' faces painted to symbolise the type of character they are playing?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kathakali.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In "Kathakali", the classical dance-drama of Kerala, the actors' faces are elaborately painted (make-up) to symbolise the type of character they play (e.g., Pacha/green for noble heroes, Kathi for villains). (कथकली — चेहरे की रंगाई)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Kathakali is known for its huge, colourful costumes, headgear and detailed facial make-up; it is largely performed by men and enacts stories from the Ramayana and Mahabharata.

• The make-up colours: Pacha (green) = virtuous, Kathi = villainous, Thadi = bearded types, Kari (black) = demonesses.

NOTE

• The eight classical dances: Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (North India), Kathakali & Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur), Sattriya (Assam).

question: In 1992, which organisation launched Self Help Group – Bank Linkage Programme?
solution_text:
The correct answer is NABARD.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In 1992, "NABARD (National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development)" launched the Self Help Group – Bank Linkage Programme (SHG-BLP) to connect informal Self Help Groups with the formal banking system for credit. (नाबार्ड — स्वयं सहायता समूह-बैंक लिंकेज कार्यक्रम)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The SHG-Bank Linkage Programme is the largest microfinance programme in the world, promoting financial inclusion, especially among rural women.

• NABARD was established in 1982 as the apex bank for rural and agricultural credit.

NOTE

• Regulators/apex bodies: SEBI (securities market), RBI (central bank & monetary policy), NABARD (rural/agriculture refinance), SIDBI (small industries).

question: In which of the following states is the Bhadaravi Poonam Mela organised every year in the Nilkanth Mahadev temple premises in Babra?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gujarat.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Bhadaravi Poonam Mela" (also linked with the Ambaji fair) is organised every year in Gujarat. The question notes its association with the Nilkanth Mahadev temple premises in Babra. (गुजरात — भादरवी पूनम मेला)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The famous Bhadarvi Poonam Mela at Ambaji (Banaskantha, Gujarat) is one of the largest religious fairs in India, held on the full moon of the Bhadrapada month.

• Ambaji is one of the 51 Shakti Peethas, dedicated to Goddess Amba/Shakti.

NOTE

• Major fairs of India: Kumbh Mela (UP/Uttarakhand/MP), Pushkar Fair (Rajasthan), Sonepur Mela (Bihar), Ambaji/Bhadarvi Poonam Mela (Gujarat).

question: As per the Constitution (Ninety-First Amendment) Act, 2003, the total number of ministers, including the Prime Minister, shall NOT exceed:
option_1: 20% of the total number of members of the Lok Sabha
option_2: 15% of the total number of members of the Lok Sabha
option_3: 10% of the total number of members of the Lok Sabha
option_4: 25% of the total number of members of the Lok Sabha
solution_text:
The correct answer is 15% of the total number of members of the Lok Sabha.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the Constitution (Ninety-First Amendment) Act, 2003, the total number of Ministers, including the Prime Minister, in the Council of Ministers shall NOT exceed 15% of the total number of members of the Lok Sabha. (91वां संविधान संशोधन — 15%)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The same 15% ceiling applies to the states (Article 164(1A)), but a state's Council of Ministers must have a minimum of 12 ministers.

• The 91st Amendment (2003) also strengthened the Anti-Defection Law (Tenth Schedule) by barring defectors from holding ministerial office.

NOTE

• Relevant Articles: Article 75(1A) (size of Union Council of Ministers) and Article 164(1A) (size in states).

question: Which of the following cities is known as the Steel City in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jamshedpur.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Jamshedpur" (in Jharkhand) is known as the "Steel City" of India. It grew around the Tata Iron and Steel Company (TISCO/Tata Steel), established in 1907 by Jamsetji Nusserwanji Tata. (जमशेदपुर — स्टील सिटी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Jamshedpur is also called "Tatanagar" and is regarded as the first planned industrial city of India.

• Other steel cities: Bhilai (Chhattisgarh), Bokaro (Jharkhand), Rourkela (Odisha), Durgapur (West Bengal).

NOTE

• City nicknames: Bengaluru – Silicon Valley of India; Detroit of India – Chennai; Manchester of India – Ahmedabad; Steel City – Jamshedpur.

question: Indian classical musician, Ustad Rashid Khan was awarded the Padma Bhushan in 2022 for his contribution to which of the following music categories?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Hindustani classical music.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Ustad Rashid Khan was awarded the Padma Bhushan in 2022 for his contribution to Hindustani classical music. He belonged to the Rampur–Sahaswan gharana. (हिंदुस्तानी शास्त्रीय संगीत)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Ustad Rashid Khan was famous for his khayal and thumri renditions; he passed away in January 2024.

• He was earlier honoured with the Padma Shri (2006) and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award.

NOTE

• Indian classical music has two main streams: Hindustani (North India) and Carnatic (South India). Padma awards: Padma Vibhushan > Padma Bhushan > Padma Shri.

question: In a metro station, it was observed that on an average 20 people per minute were using the escalator to reach at a height of 15 metres. Calculate the power of the escalator assuming the average mass of people to be 50 kg and acceleration due to gravity to be 10 m/s2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2.5 kW.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Power = Work done / time. Work done in lifting people = mgh (gain in potential energy).

◦ In 1 minute (60 s), 20 people are lifted, total mass = 20 × 50 = 1000 kg.

◦ Work = m g h = 1000 × 10 × 15 = 1,50,000 J.

◦ Power = Work / time = 1,50,000 ÷ 60 = 2500 W = 2.5 kW.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Power is the rate of doing work; SI unit is the watt (W); 1 kW = 1000 W.

• Potential energy = mgh, where m = mass, g = 10 m/s², h = height.

NOTE

• Useful relations: 1 horsepower (hp) ≈ 746 W; 1 kWh = 3.6 × 10⁶ J (the "unit" of electricity).

question: When was the Ustad Bismillah Khan Yuva Puraskar, an award given by the Sangeet Natak Akademi to outstanding artists under 40 who have demonstrated talent in the fields of music, dance and theatre, started?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2006.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Ustad Bismillah Khan Yuva Puraskar" was started in 2006 by the Sangeet Natak Akademi. It is given to outstanding young artists (under 40 years) in the fields of music, dance and theatre. (उस्ताद बिस्मिल्लाह खान युवा पुरस्कार — 2006)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• It is named after the legendary shehnai maestro Ustad Bismillah Khan, who was awarded the Bharat Ratna (2001).

• The Sangeet Natak Akademi (established 1952) is India's national academy for music, dance and drama.

NOTE

• Highest honour of the Akademi is the Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowship (Ratna Sadasya); the Akademi Award is given for lifetime achievement.

question: Who among the following was the pioneer of 'Bhoodan Movement'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Acharya Vinoba Bhave.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Bhoodan Movement" (Land Gift Movement) was pioneered by Acharya Vinoba Bhave in 1951, starting from Pochampally village (Telangana). It appealed to landowners to voluntarily donate land to the landless. (आचार्य विनोबा भावे — भूदान आंदोलन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Vinoba Bhave was a follower of Mahatma Gandhi and was chosen by him as the first individual Satyagrahi (1940).

• The movement later expanded into the "Gramdan" (village-gift) movement.

NOTE

• Vinoba Bhave was the first recipient of the Ramon Magsaysay Award (1958) and was posthumously awarded the Bharat Ratna (1983).

question: In Dholavira, which of the following materials is extensively used as a building material?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Stone.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• At "Dholavira" (a Harappan site in Gujarat, in the Rann of Kutch), stone was extensively used as a building material, unlike most other Harappan sites that mainly used baked/mud bricks. (धौलावीरा — पत्थर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Dholavira is famous for its excellent water management system (reservoirs, dams), a unique three-part city plan (citadel, middle town, lower town) and a large signboard with Indus script.

• It was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2021.

NOTE

• Major Harappan sites: Harappa & Mohenjo-daro (Pakistan), Lothal, Dholavira, Rakhigarhi, Kalibangan, Ropar (India). Rakhigarhi (Haryana) is the largest Harappan site in India.

question: The concept of Concurrent List in the Indian Constitution is borrowed from the Constitution of _____________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Australia.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The concept of the "Concurrent List" in the Indian Constitution is borrowed from the Constitution of Australia. Both the Centre and the States can legislate on the subjects in this list. (समवर्ती सूची — ऑस्ट्रेलिया से)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Seventh Schedule of the Constitution has three lists: Union List, State List and Concurrent List.

• In case of a conflict on a Concurrent List subject, the Union law prevails (Article 254).

NOTE

• Borrowed features: Fundamental Rights, Judicial Review (USA); Parliamentary system, Rule of Law (Britain); Concurrent List, Freedom of Trade (Australia); Directive Principles (Ireland); Fundamental Duties, Planning (USSR).

question: What is the rank of Sri Lanka in the Global Hunger Index (GHI) 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 60.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the Global Hunger Index (GHI) 2023, Sri Lanka was ranked 60th among the countries assessed. (वैश्विक भूख सूचकांक 2023 — श्रीलंका 60वें स्थान पर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• India was ranked 111 out of 125 countries in the GHI 2023, placing it in the "serious" category.

• The GHI is jointly published by Concern Worldwide (Ireland) and Welthungerhilfe (Germany).

NOTE

• The GHI is measured on four indicators: undernourishment, child stunting, child wasting and child mortality. Lower score/rank = less hunger.

question: What is the primary acid found in citrus fruits like oranges and lemons?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Citric acid.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The primary acid found in citrus fruits like oranges and lemons is "citric acid", which gives them their sour/tangy taste. (साइट्रिक अम्ल — नींबू, संतरा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Lactic acid – found in curd/milk (sour milk) and muscles.

• Tartaric acid – found in tamarind and grapes.

• Acetic acid – found in vinegar.

NOTE

• Other natural acids: Malic acid (apple), Oxalic acid (tomato/spinach), Formic acid (ant sting/bee), Citric acid (citrus fruits).

question: In which state are the Gua and Noamundi iron ore mines located?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jharkhand.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Gua" and "Noamundi" iron ore mines are located in the West Singhbhum district of Jharkhand. Noamundi is one of the oldest mechanised iron ore mines in India, operated by Tata Steel. (झारखंड — गुआ और नोआमुंडी लौह अयस्क खदानें)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Jharkhand is very rich in minerals — iron ore, coal, mica, copper and uranium.

• India's major iron ore belts also lie in Odisha, Chhattisgarh and Karnataka (Bellary–Hospet).

NOTE

• Types of iron ore: Magnetite (best quality, ~72% iron), Hematite (most used commercially), Limonite and Siderite.

question: The climatic diversity of India is characterised by its distinctiveness, and one of the following factors does NOT contribute to it is ______________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is longitudinal extent.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Among the given options, "longitudinal extent" does NOT significantly contribute to India's climatic diversity. Longitude mainly affects time (local time differences), not climate. Climate is more influenced by latitude, topography (relief) and vegetation. (देशांतरीय विस्तार — जलवायु को प्रभावित नहीं करता)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Latitudinal extent affects temperature (the Tropic of Cancer passes through the middle of India).

• Topography (Himalayas, Western Ghats) blocks/directs winds and rainfall; vegetation affects local humidity and temperature.

NOTE

• Key controls of Indian climate: latitude, altitude, pressure & winds (monsoons), distance from the sea, ocean currents and relief (topography).

question: The rock-cut temple of Shiva built by Krishna I is found at which of the following places?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ellora.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The famous rock-cut Kailasa Temple of Shiva, built by the Rashtrakuta king Krishna I, is found at "Ellora" (in Maharashtra). It is carved out of a single rock. (एलोरा — कैलाश मंदिर, कृष्ण प्रथम)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Kailasa Temple (Cave 16) at Ellora is the world's largest monolithic rock-cut structure.

• The Ellora Caves (Buddhist, Hindu and Jain) are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

NOTE

• The Rashtrakutas (8th–10th century CE) had their capital at Manyakheta; Ellora and the Elephanta Caves are among their greatest architectural legacies.

question: Consider the following statements in the context of the Vedas. 1.The Vedas are called Shruti. 2.The Rigveda consists of ten Mandalas. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both 1 and 2.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Statement 1 is correct: The Vedas are called "Shruti" ("that which is heard"), as they were traditionally transmitted orally.

• Statement 2 is correct: The Rigveda consists of ten Mandalas (books). Hence both statements are correct. (दोनों कथन सही — वेद 'श्रुति', ऋग्वेद में 10 मंडल)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The four Vedas: Rigveda (hymns), Samaveda (melodies/chants), Yajurveda (sacrificial formulae), Atharvaveda (spells and charms).

• The Rigveda is the oldest Veda; its 3rd Mandala contains the Gayatri Mantra.

NOTE

• Vedic literature is classified as Shruti (Vedas, Brahmanas, Aranyakas, Upanishads) and Smriti (Puranas, epics, Dharmashastras).

question: Which Article of the Constitution of India provides provision for appointment of the same person as the Governor for two or more states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 153.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Article 153" of the Constitution provides that there shall be a Governor for each State; a proviso added by the 7th Amendment (1956) allows the same person to be appointed as the Governor for two or more states. (अनुच्छेद 153)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Article 155 – Governor is appointed by the President.

• Article 156 – tenure of the Governor (holds office during the pleasure of the President; normally 5 years).

• Article 157 – qualifications; Article 158 – conditions of the Governor's office.

NOTE

• The Governor is the constitutional head of a state (Articles 153–162). The office was borrowed from the Government of India Act, 1935 / Canadian model.

question: In which of the following year did India win the ICC T20 Men's Cricket World Cup?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2007.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• India won the first-ever ICC T20 Men's Cricket World Cup in 2007, held in South Africa, defeating Pakistan in the final. The team was captained by Mahendra Singh Dhoni. (2007 — पहला टी20 विश्व कप, भारत विजेता)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• In the 2007 final, Joginder Sharma bowled the decisive last over; Yuvraj Singh famously hit six sixes in an over off Stuart Broad in that tournament.

• India won the T20 World Cup again in 2024 (in the West Indies & USA), captained by Rohit Sharma.

NOTE

• India's World Cup wins: 1983 & 2011 (ODI World Cup) and 2007 & 2024 (T20 World Cup); also the 2013 Champions Trophy.

question: Which of the following government initiatives focuses on skill development to reduce open unemployment among youth in India?
option_2: Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA)
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY).

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY)" focuses on skill development to make the youth employable and reduce open unemployment. It was launched in 2015 under the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship. (प्रधानमंत्री कौशल विकास योजना)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• PM KUSUM – promotes solar energy for farmers.

• MGNREGA (2005) – guarantees 100 days of wage employment in rural areas.

• Swachh Bharat Abhiyan (2014) – cleanliness and sanitation mission.

NOTE

• PMKVY is implemented by the National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC); it offers Short-Term Training and Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL).

question: How many titles did West Bengal win in the Santosh Trophy events up to the 2022-23 season?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 32.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Up to the 2022–23 season, West Bengal had won the Santosh Trophy a record 32 times, making it the most successful team in the tournament. (संतोष ट्रॉफी — पश्चिम बंगाल, 32 खिताब)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Santosh Trophy is a national football championship contested by state associations and government institutions, started in 1941.

• It is named after Sir Manmatha Nath Roy Chowdhary of Santosh (now in Bangladesh).

NOTE

• Indian football bodies: AIFF (All India Football Federation) governs the game; the top club league is the Indian Super League (ISL).

question: Who among the following Governor-Generals declared 'Sati' practice as illegal?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lord William Bentinck.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Lord William Bentinck" declared the practice of "Sati" as illegal through the Bengal Sati Regulation Act of 1829. He was supported in this reform by Raja Ram Mohan Roy. (लॉर्ड विलियम बेंटिंक — सती प्रथा उन्मूलन, 1829)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Lord William Bentinck was the first Governor-General of India (1833–35) under the Charter Act of 1833.

• Other reforms in his time: suppression of Thuggee (with William Sleeman) and promotion of English education (Macaulay's Minute, 1835).

NOTE

• Lord Canning – last Governor-General & first Viceroy (Revolt of 1857); Lord Dalhousie – Doctrine of Lapse, railways; Lord Lytton – Vernacular Press Act, 1878.

question: Which of the following fictional towns is mentioned in the English novel 'In Custody' written by Anita Desai?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mirpore.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The fictional town "Mirpore" is mentioned in the novel "In Custody" written by Anita Desai (published 1984). The story follows a Hindi lecturer, Deven, and an Urdu poet, Nur. (मिरपोर — 'इन कस्टडी', अनीता देसाई)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• "In Custody" was shortlisted for the Booker Prize and later made into a film by Merchant–Ivory.

• Anita Desai is a noted Indian novelist; her works include Fire on the Mountain, Clear Light of Day and The Village by the Sea.

NOTE

• Famous fictional Indian towns: Malgudi (R. K. Narayan), Kanthapura (Raja Rao), Mirpore (Anita Desai), Lilliput (Jonathan Swift's Gulliver's Travels).

question: A particular cell present in the excretory system of flatworms, which helps them removing waste materials is the:
solution_text:
The correct answer is flame cell.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Flame cells" are the specialised excretory cells present in the excretory system of flatworms (Platyhelminthes) and some other invertebrates. They help remove waste materials and excess water (osmoregulation). (फ्लेम कोशिका — चपटे कृमि का उत्सर्जन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Flame cells are part of the protonephridia; the beating of their cilia (resembling a flickering flame) drives fluid through the system.

• In earthworms, the excretory organs are nephridia; in humans, the excretory unit is the nephron (in kidneys).

NOTE

• Cnidoblasts (nematocysts) are the stinging cells of Cnidaria (Hydra, jellyfish); passage cells occur in the endodermis of plant roots.
